synopsis: Chapter 12 attributes the formalization of reference class forecasting to Flyvbjerg (2006; 2008; with Gardner, 2023): estimating from actual outcomes of comparable past projects rather than the current plan’s internal details, to counter optimism bias and strategic misrepresentation [f9604]. The glossary connects this method to Kahneman and Lovallo’s “outside view” and adds that estimates from comparable projects are then adjusted [f16313]. Chapter 12 also associates reference class forecasting plus schedule-risk analysis with Flyvbjerg 2006 and GAO-16-89G [f10062]. The behavioural explanation of cost overruns remains disputed: Love and Ahiaga-Dagbui challenged it in 2018, while Flyvbjerg and colleagues defended it; the practical value of reference class forecasting is described as less contested than its mechanism [f9610, f10317, f10318]. However, Chapter 13 says this literature was not verified in the research and treats reference class forecasting as a relevant lead rather than a verified basis for planning [f10743, f11199].
